clue.text: Edible plant American fools spotted in flower

indicators.note: spotted in says one thing is seen sitting inside the other, so the fools go into the flower

parts.note: the iris is a garden flower
shmo (schmo) is American slang for a fool, plural shmos

explanation.surface: Some foolish Americans are seen among the flowers, next to an edible plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted in' signals the insertion. Irish moss is carrageen, a red seaweed eaten in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrageen, a red seaweed used as food and to set puddings, goes by this name.

clue.text: Popular writer has to engross

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A best-selling author has to absorb readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engross' looks like absorb, but its older sense is to write out a document in large formal script.
explanation.definitionFit: To write out a legal document in a large clear hand is to letter it formally.

clue.text: On current form, is a leading person in race

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Judging by current form, he is the front runner in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' only joins. The race is a people, not a contest: Isaac, son of Abraham, was a patriarch of the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac was one of the three patriarchs from whom the Hebrew people descend.

clue.text: Left to sit here, child gets fed up

definitions.text: Left to sit here, child gets fed up

parts.words: Left to sit here, child gets fed up
parts.note: fed up reads as bored, but it means given meals while raised up off the floor, in a tall seat

explanation.surface: A child left sitting alone becomes bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' is fed while up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat with a tray, in which an infant sits for meals at table height.

clue.text: Fabulous musician whose comeback ended in disaster

definitions.text: Fabulous musician whose comeback ended in disaster

parts.words: Fabulous musician whose comeback ended in disaster
parts.note: fabulous means of fable: the lyre player of Greek myth looked back while leading his wife out of the underworld and lost her

explanation.surface: A fabulous pop star's return tour flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reads as a return to the stage; it is the backward glance at Eurydice.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Thracian lyre player of Greek myth lost his wife by glancing behind him.

clue.text: Sign crop is transformed by oxygen

indicators.note: transformed says these letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A harvest is altered by adding oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is transformed' rearranges CROPIS into SCORPI; 'is' is also fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorpion is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Withdraw quote about husband's moral principles

indicators.note: about says the turned-round quote goes round the husband's letter
withdraw read as draw back: the word for quote is turned backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
H is the usual abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a remark about a husband's morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' turns CITE into ETIC, and 'about' puts H inside it. A plural definition for a singular noun is loose, but ethic is often used for a set of principles.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a code of right conduct, the set of values governing how someone behaves.

clue.text: Cockney gardener's tool for trimming border

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: a hedger is a gardener who trims hedges

explanation.surface: An East End gardener owns a tool for neatening the lawn's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners known for dropping the h.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with a half-moon blade cuts a neat line where lawn meets flower bed.

clue.text: One attempting to cure in old way

parts.note: at home means in, not out
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A healer clings to traditional remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in old way' reads as old-fashioned treatment, but it is three pieces: HOME for in (as in 'staying in'), O for old, PATH for way.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of the alternative system treating illness with tiny doses of substances causing similar symptoms.

clue.text: American agency retaining staff, mounting pictures here

indicators.note: retaining says the agency's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means rising, so the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: staff are men, the workforce

explanation.surface: A US intelligence agency keeping staff on puts up pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns staff upwards and 'retaining' puts it inside the agency. 'Pictures' is the British word for films.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is British slang for the movies, so a picture house shows them.

clue.text: Attack on south extended north of the border

parts.note: north of the border is Scotland, where long (extended) is said lang

explanation.surface: An assault on the south is prolonged up into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland to British readers; the Scots form of long is lang, as in Auld Lang Syne.
explanation.definitionFit: To slang someone is to abuse them verbally, a spoken assault.

clue.text: One can't keep control of shares when lunching, however

definitions.text: One can't keep control of shares when lunching, however

parts.words: One can't keep control of shares when lunching, however
parts.note: shares are ploughshares, the blades of a plough, which its driver cannot steer while he stops for the cheese-and-pickle meal named after him

explanation.surface: An investor loses grip on his portfolio over a long lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial sense of shares misleads: they are ploughshares. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm worker who drives a plough cannot steer its blades while stopped to eat.

clue.text: Salvage bike engineers put in van

indicators.note: van means the front, so the engineers are put at the start, before the bike

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: Someone saves a bicycle that mechanics have loaded into a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' is not the vehicle but vanguard, the front: 'put in van' puts the engineers first.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage material is to reclaim it for reuse, which is what reprocessing waste does.

clue.text: Put on a show for each class

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Each school class stages a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a theatrical display or act on stage is to put on a show.

clue.text: Break for worker, making him busy and also working?

indicators.note: working read as being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker's time off keeps him busy and still on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges HIMBUSYANDALSO into the answer; the question mark admits the surface also describes the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for leisure time spent doing much the same as one's job, as a bus driver taking a coach trip.

clue.text: Champion appears to drink beer

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: The winner looks as if he is having a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of a cause is one who backs or advocates it.

clue.text: Wild animal I caught on both sides of island

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the eland is a large African antelope
the same abbreviation used for the second side

explanation.surface: I trapped a wild beast on both sides of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on both sides' puts I and C (I caught) both before and after ELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things belonging to the North Atlantic nation of Iceland.

clue.text: Shot bagging an eagle, perhaps, if perfectly executed

definitions.text: Shot bagging an eagle, perhaps, if perfectly executed

parts.words: Shot bagging an eagle, perhaps, if perfectly executed
parts.note: bagging an eagle reads as hunting a bird, but an eagle is two under par in golf, and a shot to the green that drops in can score one

explanation.surface: A hunter's shot brings down an eagle with a perfect hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunting picture misleads: this is golf, where holing the shot played onto the green can give an eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, the stroke played towards the green from the fairway is so named.

clue.text: One is bound, in time, to learn from this

definitions.text: One is bound, in time, to learn from this

parts.words: One is bound, in time, to learn from this
parts.note: bound reads as certain, but it means bound by indentures to a master for a fixed term, during which a trade is learned

explanation.surface: Sooner or later everyone learns a lesson from this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is bound' looks like 'is sure to'; it means tied by an indenture, and 'in time' is the fixed term of service.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee bound by contract to a master learns a trade over a fixed period of service.

clue.text: In enables meals to be taken on the trot

definitions.text: In enables meals to be taken on the trot

parts.words: In enables meals to be taken on the trot
parts.note: on the trot reads as on the go, but it means while a horse is moving, eating from a feed sack hung on its head

explanation.surface: Something lets people eat on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is evidently a misprint for 'It' on the printed page. 'On the trot' is British for on the go, but trotting horses are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A feed bag hung over a horse's muzzle lets it eat while working.

clue.text: Intuitive 'understanding available to viewers

definitions.meaning: a deep grasp of something, seen without reasoning

explanation.walkthrough: The stray quote mark is an OCR artefact; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perception of a truth, and in sight means within view.

clue.text: Bad temper produced by endless disease

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: cholera is an infectious intestinal disease

explanation.surface: An infection leaves someone irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler was one of the four humours, linked with anger, hence irritability.

clue.text: Smoking apparatus a husband secures outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for secures sits round the other letters

parts.note: to hook something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: A husband's water pipe is fastened up outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts HOOKS round A and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Water pipes that draw tobacco smoke through water are smoking devices.

clue.text: This ruler's a male, invariably

parts.note: e'er, poetic for ever, means always

explanation.surface: This monarch is, without exception, a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir, an Islamic prince or governor, is also spelt this way.

clue.text: One who shoots large fish

definitions.meaning: a press photographer who takes pictures, a shooter with a camera
a sizeable sea fish of warm waters, prized as food

explanation.definitionFit: A photographer snaps pictures, and the red snapper is a sizeable food fish.

clue.text: Lively dance a president leads off

indicators.note: leads off says the president comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: James K. Polk was the eleventh US president

explanation.surface: A president opens the ball with a lively number.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Untidy lout in bed with infection

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
a bug is an infection, as in a stomach bug

explanation.surface: A slovenly yob lies in bed with an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drops rubbish in public places is an untidy lout.

clue.text: A little model taking wing

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small model aircraft takes flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' tells you only part of 'model taking' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular aircraft wing, named from the Greek letter's shape, is a delta wing.

clue.text: It's not so usual, having basic education at regular intervals

definitions.text: It's not so usual, having basic education at regular intervals

parts.words: It's not so usual, having basic education at regular intervals
parts.note: basic education is the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic; the word meaning less common has an R in every other place

explanation.surface: Schooling only at set intervals is becoming less common.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part defines; the rest describes the word: R, A, R, E, R holds three Rs at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Less common or found less often is the comparative of uncommon.

clue.text: Restrict movements of Conservative silly enough to join party improperly

parts.note: to gate a student is to confine them to college as a punishment
rash means foolishly hasty, silly

explanation.surface: A foolish Tory is confined as punishment for barging into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is a British school and university punishment: being kept within the gates.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a social event uninvited is to crash it.
